function.name: irpt-performance-adapter
function.mechanism_note: The yang-lambda module sets s3_object_version = data.aws_s3_object.artifact.version_id and source_code_hash = that object's content-sha256 metadata (module main.tf:17,38,39), and the data source reads the LATEST version of the key. So the rollback could NOT be done by re-pointing Terraform at version 7IkeCAOa8F8IzqgaW1_WCLczFhmtzaLn; the latest version had to become one carrying the pre-release bytes. That version was re-read first as still present with content-sha256 9kYLdR64... and 445438 bytes, then the restored source-map entry was rebuilt -- BUILD_ONLY printed 9kYLdR64..., which is the proof the restored entry reproduces the pre-release bytes -- and uploaded as a NEW version with the same digest and size. The pre-release package is therefore live by CONTENT, which is what the order's after-read requires.

targeted_destroy_plan.deviation_from_the_order: The order's two -target flags alone were REFUSED by Terraform: 'Moved resource instances excluded by targeting', naming the two additional targets to add. Restoring retained.tf restored the count meta-argument on all four session blocks, so each applied object's address moved from the un-indexed form to the count-indexed [0] form, and the two DATA sources moved with the two policies. The plan was re-run with the two policy targets PLUS data.aws_secretsmanager_secret.performance_cot_session and data.aws_secretsmanager_secret.performance_inf_session, exactly as Terraform's own error instructed; its alternative, dropping targeting altogether, would have been less targeted rather than more. Those two are data sources which, with count now 0, are removed from state and not read; even when read they resolve a secret NAME to an ARN and never a secret VALUE. The count gate still governed and was exact. Recorded because it changed HOW the plan was produced, not what landed.
targeted_destroy_plan.destroy_annotations: each policy at index [0], 'because index [0] is out of range for count' and 'moved from' its un-indexed address, each showing its single secretsmanager:GetSecretValue statement removed; no other resource action

fresh_request.how: OPTION TWO of the order's two, recorded as the order requires. This seat cannot drive a caller the function ADMITS, because a synthetic principal cannot supply a verified internal subject -- which is precisely why IB-pr-423's live-call arm could not have caught the defect this rollback undoes. So the request is the IDENTICAL event used as IB-pr-423's live call (routeKey GET /api/scoped/investor-reporting/performance/{accountSetId}, non-49F X-Firm-Id cottonwood), plus the prescribed read of the function's log from the rollback promote on.

full_root_plan: No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration. -- confirmed machine-readably as well as in prose: the same plan with -detailed-exitcode returns rc=0, where 0 is no-changes and 2 would be changes-pending, so the verdict does not rest on matching a sentence. This is the same reading the IB-pr-422 packet recorded for the UNEDITED tree before the release.

served_while_live.use_record_note: Stated as NOT READ rather than as zero. PERFORMANCE_USE# appears 0 times in the LOG GROUP, but the use record is a DynamoDB PutItem into the requests table, which a log read does not reach; 0 log occurrences is therefore not evidence of 0 records written. The order explicitly asks for 'not read' where the read does not reach.
served_while_live.corroboration: The served_count of 3 matches the escalation's independent count of three served at 09:45Z.
served_while_live.preserved: Per the order's bound, neither the retained vendor reports nor the use records written while the release was live were deleted or altered: they are the record of what was served.

tests_after_restore.why_it_matters: This is the test the COO half recorded as row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W282-S3, writing 'It was NOT run on the pre-change tree, so pre-existing is inferred'. CTO condition 4 asked for it to be run on the pre-change tree so pre-existing is MEASURED. The rollback restored exactly that tree, so this run IS that measurement: the failure is present with the release absent, making it pre-existing as fact rather than inference. It imports none of the five modules the release touched.
tests_after_restore.count_check: The COO half read 1 failed, 268 passed on the release tree; the pre-change tree reads 1 failed, 251 passed. The 17-test difference is the release's own tests, gone with it.

method: Every digest was read from the LIVE function or from the S3 object's own content-sha256 metadata, never from the builder's stdout alone. The role was read back from the LIVE role twice over: list-role-policies for the set and count, and get-role-policy per removed name for an explicit NoSuchEntity. Both log windows were read with filter-log-events, auto-paginated and counted client-side with the denominator printed. No vendor was called and no secretsmanager get-secret-value was run at any point in this act. Counts, digests, status and reason codes only: no account id, balance or figure appears here.
